subject.title: [Bug]: Slack `allowBots: true` silently drops all bot messages unless `allowFrom` contains an explicit owner user ID

question: Should Slack wildcard-only `allowFrom` configurations ever admit bot-authored room messages when `allowBots` is enabled, or should OpenClaw preserve explicit-owner presence and only warn unless an explicit unsafe mode is approved?
rationale: The current behavior is a documented security fix for bot relays, but it silently breaks real Slack automation workflows; choosing between fail-closed security, diagnostics, and a new all-bot mode needs maintainer security intent.

options.title: Warn and preserve guard
options.body: Add Slack config/doctor/startup diagnostics for wildcard-only or ownerless `allowBots` setups while keeping explicit owner presence or channel bot allowlists required for room bot messages.

options.title: Add explicit all-bot mode
options.body: Accept a new clearly named opt-in mode that skips the room authorization gate, with security wording and regression/live proof for guarded and unguarded modes.

options.title: Treat wildcard as presence
options.body: Make wildcard `allowFrom` satisfy the bot-room gate, restoring intuitive wildcard behavior but weakening the prior owner-presence security boundary for existing configs.

recommendation.title: Warn and preserve guard
recommendation.body: Add Slack config/doctor/startup diagnostics for wildcard-only or ownerless `allowBots` setups while keeping explicit owner presence or channel bot allowlists required for room bot messages.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and documented the owner-presence guard that this issue asks maintainers to preserve, warn about, or relax.
